name: Lip suction pump
lead: A lip suction pump is a hand-held vacuum device placed over the lips to make them look fuller. Wikipedia's lip plumper article describes such devices as using vacuum pumping to raise blood pressure in the lips, causing temporary swelling.[1]
It is one of several non-injection plumping approaches, alongside topical plumpers whose irritant ingredients such as capsaicin cause swelling.[1] Published information on the devices is sparse.

paras: The device creates suction over the lips, which Wikipedia describes as drawing blood into the tissue and producing short-lived swelling.[1]
Wikipedia does not list risks specific to suction devices; its risk section covers injectable and surgical procedures.[1]

card.summary: A vacuum cup that temporarily swells the lips; no studies found.
card.note: Effect described as temporary swelling; no research found.

quick.overview:

No studies of it were found; only a brief description in an encyclopedia.
quick.mechanism: Wikipedia describes the vacuum as raising blood pressure in the lips, causing temporary swelling.
quick.risks: No risks specific to the device are documented in the sources found.
